## Investigation Report

### Verdict/Confidence/Severity/Task Type

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Verdict | Confirmed partial fix with remaining policy-safety and diagnostics gaps |
| Confidence | High |
| Severity | High |
| Task Type | Verification-policy correctness and fail-closed setup hardening |

### What Was Claimed

Issue #94 reports that a schema-valid required command such as root `npm test` can survive setup and only fail after implementation because the policy cannot express a monorepo package directory. The requested behavior is an explicit validated working directory, static preflight before any writer, actionable policy-path diagnostics, safe `/forge:init` behavior, monorepo regression coverage, and unchanged fail-closed verification.

### What We Found

The frozen base already contains a substantial implementation: `VerificationCommandPolicy.cwd` defaults to `.`, policy parsing rejects absolute paths, traversal, backslashes, and NUL bytes, and `verification-preflight.ts` resolves symlinks, checks executable availability, and inspects `package.json` scripts without running them. `startIssue` performs that preflight against the prepared integration worktree before agent materialization or child dispatch and cleans up if preflight fails. A monorepo fixture already covers root-without-`test` versus `web`-with-`test`.

Two gaps remain. First, preflight failures do not consistently include a concrete remediation that names the exact tracked policy path and `/forge:init` or a config edit; directory, executable, and malformed-manifest failures are less actionable than the missing-script case. Second, `/forge:init` always replaces existing tracked local commands with `{}`. That silently weakens a valid required local policy when setup is rerun, rather than preserving the approved command/cwd binding; new template setup is already explicit CI-only because it starts with an empty command map.

### Root Cause

The partial fix added command `cwd` and a preflight adapter but left setup serialization destructive and diagnostics inconsistent. The preflight path is correct for the direct `npm test`/`npm run <script>` forms, but its error contract was not normalized around the policy path and remediation.

### Affected Files

| File | Concern |
|---|---|
| `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` | Normalize actionable remediation for every static preflight failure |
| `src/ui/commands.ts` | Preserve existing validated command bindings during `/forge:init`; make CI-only status visible |
| `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` | Regression coverage for exact policy paths and remediation |
| `test/ui/commands.test.ts` | Setup serialization regression coverage where the command configuration helper is exposed/testable |

### Evidence

- `src/core/policy.ts` defines `cwd`, applies a repository-relative normalizer, and defaults omitted values to `.`.
- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` checks required commands only, uses `shell: false` downstream, resolves cwd symlinks, and statically reads package scripts.
- `src/workflows/work-on.ts` calls `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands(prepared.worktreePath, policy.verification.commands, ...)` before `materializeForgeAgents` and `spawnWorkOn`.
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` proves root `npm test` is rejected while `web` `npm test` passes and that no command is executed during preflight.
- `src/ui/commands.ts` currently assigns `verification.commands: {}` while rebuilding the tracked policy.

### History Findings

No separate history artifact is available in the bound task context. The frozen-base source and tests demonstrate that cwd/preflight work was introduced before this run; this implementation will close the remaining setup-preservation and diagnostic gaps without changing the trusted command model.

### Recommendation

Keep the existing validated cwd/preflight contract. Add a shared remediation formatter so missing directories, executables, package manifests, invalid JSON, and scripts all report the full config path plus a concrete edit or `/forge:init` CI-only option. Preserve the existing command map in `/forge:init` instead of silently clearing it, and report whether local commands or GitHub-CI-only verification are configured. Add focused tests for these guarantees while retaining the existing monorepo and fail-closed coverage.

### Related Issues

- Issue #94 — required verification policy is not preflighted for monorepos.

### Decomposition Assessment

The work is bounded to policy setup serialization, static preflight diagnostics, and regression tests. No product, UX, protected-branch, security-authority, or cross-repository decision is required.

### Acceptance Spec

- [x] A validated repository-relative `cwd` binds commands to monorepo packages.
- [x] Required executable, package directory, manifest, and script checks occur statically before writer dispatch.
- [ ] Every preflight failure names its exact tracked config path and concrete remediation.
- [ ] `/forge:init` preserves an existing command/cwd map and explicitly reports CI-only mode for empty commands.
- [x] Root-without-script and package-with-script regression fixture remains covered.
- [x] Required command execution remains fail-closed after implementation.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

## Builder Contract

### Allowed Files

- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts`
- `src/ui/commands.ts`
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts`
- `test/ui/commands.test.ts` only if a pure setup-status helper requires direct coverage

### Allowed Symbols and Behaviors

- Add or refine deterministic remediation text emitted by `VerificationPreflightError`.
- Keep required-command checks static: executable availability, safe cwd resolution, package manifest parsing, and script presence; never execute repository code during preflight.
- Preserve repository-relative cwd validation, symlink containment, and shell-free runtime execution.
- Preserve existing tracked verification command/cwd bindings when `/forge:init` rewrites unrelated policy fields; an empty template remains explicit GitHub-CI-only verification.
- Make init's resulting local-verification mode visible in its completion notification.
- Add regression assertions for exact config-path diagnostics and command preservation/status behavior.

### Forbidden Changes

- No arbitrary shell, new verification names, command execution during preflight, or relaxation of required-check failure handling.
- No changes to GitHub authentication, state authority, leases, worktree ownership, reviewer policy, branch protection, merge/close behavior, or user issue scope.
- No edits outside the allowed files.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Required preflight failures identify the exact tracked config path and a concrete config edit or `/forge:init` CI-only remediation.
- [ ] `/forge:init` does not silently discard existing local command/cwd policy; empty new setup remains CI-only and is reported.
- [ ] Monorepo root/package fixture continues to prove static script detection without executing a command.
- [ ] Required commands still execute only through the approved name and fail closed after implementation.

<!-- FORGE:CONTRACT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

The base policy parser already normalizes optional `verification.commands.<name>.cwd` to a safe repository-relative path. `preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` runs on the prepared frozen integration worktree before agent materialization and child writer dispatch. Its existing tests cover executable absence, root/package script mismatch, missing directories, control-directory rejection, and symlink escapes. The only intended code paths are diagnostic formatting and init policy serialization; no architectural seam or new authority is needed.

`configureForgePolicy` currently parses the existing policy but assigns `verification.commands: {}` while writing the updated file. Replacing that assignment with the parsed command map preserves tracked local checks; the template's command map is already empty, so first-time setup explicitly selects GitHub-CI-only verification. The completion notification can expose this state without changing interactive selection flow.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Add a small preflight remediation formatter that includes the full configured policy path and an actionable package/cwd/executable/script fix, including `/forge:init` for CI-only verification.
2. Route directory, executable, package manifest, JSON, and script failures through that formatter while preserving existing error paths and useful substrings.
3. Preserve `config.verification.commands` in `/forge:init` and add a concise local-verification status to the setup completion message.
4. Extend adapter tests for diagnostics and retain the monorepo no-script/script fixture; add only minimal UI coverage if a testable helper is introduced.
5. Run the approved `check` verification, create the implementation commit, prepare the PR, and submit a fresh correctness/security review panel at the exact frozen head.

### Risks and Mitigations

- Existing invalid commands remain visible rather than silently disabled; static preflight will fail before any writer with the new remediation.
- Diagnostic wording changes are additive so existing callers can still match the error path and failure reason.
- No command is run by the new code; tests use executable fixtures and package JSON reads only.
